title: Search the clip history from the menu
description: Type while the history menu is open to filter all clips (not just the inline ones). Matches show their history number so you can see where they are; the first match is selected so Return pastes it. Requested by the user: with 100+ clips, finding an old one by browsing folders is slow.
close_reason: Search field at the top of the history menu, focused on open; flat results with history number and folder, first match selected, Return pastes, Escape clears (via close-and-reopen). Verified by the user with ⌃⌘V.

title: Actions menu with JavaScript actions
description:
Transform a clip before pasting it, from an actions menu on a history item.

ClipMenu 0.4.3 behavior (from the decompiled app and the user's actions.plist):
- Built-in actions, e.g. "Paste as Plain Text".
- JavaScript actions: .js files that receive the clip as `clipText` and return the new text. ClipMenu bundles Case (Capitalize, lowercase, Title Case, UPPERCASE) and more under ClipMenu.app/Contents/Resources/script/action/. Scripts can call ClipMenu.require, ClipMenu.activate and prompt.
- The action list is a user-editable tree of folders and actions (actions.plist), and users can add their own scripts.
- Opened with ⌃-click on a history item (the user's ClipMenu has controlClickBehavior = popUpActionMenu).

Plan:
- Run scripts with JavaScriptCore (no WebKit) and provide clipText, ClipMenu.require/activate and prompt, so ClipMenu's existing .js actions keep working unchanged.
- Ship the bundled ClipMenu scripts' behavior as built-ins.

Decision needed: ClipShelf currently uses ⌃-click to remove an item. Moving actions to ⌃-click (ClipMenu's habit) means removal needs a new gesture (e.g. ⌃⌥-click or a submenu item).

title: Snippets: saved text in folders with their own menu
description:
Saved text that stays permanently, separate from the rolling clipboard history: sign-offs, addresses, code templates.

ClipMenu 0.4.3 behavior (from the decompiled app):
- Snippets live in folders. Each snippet has a title, content, an enabled flag and an order index; folders have a title, enabled flag and index (Core Data entities Snippet/Folder).
- A separate menu opened by its own hotkey (ClipMenu default ⇧⌘B), plus a Snippets section in the main menu.
- Selecting a snippet pastes it the same way a history item is pasted.
- An editor window to add, rename, reorder, enable/disable and delete snippets and folders.
- XML import/export (ClipMenu's Snippets.xml format).

Notes:
- The user's ClipMenu Snippets.xml is empty, so there is nothing to migrate; XML import is for compatibility only.
- Store snippets in their own file under ~/Library/Application Support/ClipShelf/, not in history.plist, so clearing history never touches them.
